~~macOS / Editor error is unrelated, may someone rerun it?~~ Thanks!
Linux / Editor with doubles and GCC sanitizers triggers https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/109158 , I'm not sure what to do here.

The error appeared only after changes, the version before them was successful.

I guess I can change atomic pointer back to a normal pointer, but I don't want to lose the certainties atomic pointer provides.

Ok, after some testing the error in the CI check `"Editor with doubles and GCC sanitizers"` appeared not because of the new atomics, but because I added a couple of lines to `_ALWAYS_INLINE_ ObjectDB::get_instance`, the test passed after removing `_ALWAYS_INLINE_`. I reproduced the error locally by building it with `gcc-11` with the same scons flags as from failed CI check and the same error had appeared. `gcc-15` on the other hand could build it normally. Well after removing always inline even `gcc-11` build it successfully. I didn't test other gcc versions.

To make sure I found the correct reason for the error I also removed a second check in `_ALWAYS_INLINE_ ObjectDB::get_instance` locally and compiled it again with `gcc-11`  and it succeeded, despite failing before it. The final version still preserves the second validator check and removes `_ALWAYS_INLINE_`, as it having always inline or not having it here doesn't affect performance, but the second validator check prevents a possible data race.

Here are the performance tests after removing `_ALWAYS_INLINE_` to show that it didn't affect performance negatively.

> ~macOS / Editor error is unrelated, may someone rerun it?~ Thanks! Linux / Editor with doubles and GCC sanitizers triggers #109158 , I'm not sure what to do here.
> 
> The error appeared only after changes, the version before them was successful.
> 
> I guess I can change atomic pointer back to a normal pointer, but I don't want to lose the certainties atomic pointer provides.

I've put a possible fix in that issue. It's likely nothing to do with this PR, except that it pushes the size over 2GB, and it's on the border already. Especially changes which bloat core in the the binary could do this.

I notice `add_instance` still has a lock. We could "give" each thread an exclusive block (via `thread_local`) to use freely so that the lock is only required when slots run out. Essentially the lock guards blocks instead of slots.

The difference is that the slots are not used incrementally across threads - I hope this isn't an issue? I also think this would extend to `remove_instance` but I'm not sure about the semantics there.

It seems possible, but I'm not confident I can do it correctly. Also for me the lock in `add_instance` can be worked around with creating needed objects beforehand, but you really can't work around using `get_instance`, so I focused on removing lock here.

And bit operations are currently compiling for testing with tsan, and I will need to recompile it again after rebase too, so changes still needs some more time.

I can try to do it after rebase. Also incrementally used slots are used for slot reuse, so I need to check if it can be used with exclusive blocks.

Agreed, `get_instance` is the more important case to optimize.

Slot reuse works like a linked list right? So it can skip across blocks without issues. Implementation wise, pretty much all the currently static fields would become thread_local except the block counter and array. Slot reuse would probably be thread specific as well (no sharing IDs across threads). Lookup is still fine though.

Thinking out loud I can only see this being a problem if an object is created in one thread and destroyed in another. Even then, the reuse should just work but slot sharing across threads would happen. This shouldn't be a problem as each slot can only ever be "owned" by one thread.

I'm not sure what the validator does and how that would work across threads without a lock.
